answer: A sybil ring lives or dies by the cost of minting identities. Make issuance quadratic: the registry links each new key to the operator's existing cluster via funding ancestry and device fingerprints, then prices the k-th identity at base times k, burned on arrival. One operator wanting 100 keys pays 10 times (100x101/2) = 50,500 tokens instead of a flat 1,000, a 50x wall. Pair it with a per-cluster earnings cap so splintering never pays back. A falcon does not outfly a falconer with a thousand decoys; the vault door just gets heavier, one copper at a time.
